name: In My Eyes
label: Revelation
lede: Anthony Pappalardo got thrown out of Ten Yard Fight and had In My Eyes going within two months, a Boston straight edge band with a rule against X imagery. It made two Revelation records and quit before it got old.

eras.title: Two months after Ten Yard Fight
eras.text: Boston was in the middle of a youth crew revival, with Ten Yard Fight, Bane and Floorpunch. Anthony Pappalardo had just been thrown out of Ten Yard Fight, and his new band set itself a few rules so it wouldn't sound like a copy of anything.

years.cap: In My Eyes flyer for 924 Gilman Street, Berkeley, August 24, 1997
q: We weren't thinking too hard, we were just doing it.
years.h: Thrown out of Ten Yard Fight, Pappalardo starts over in two months
years.p: He teams up with singer Sweet Pete, guitarist Jeff Neumann, bassist Damian Genuardi and drummer Luke Garro. The name comes from a [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] song.
years.xp:
Pappalardo says the split with Ten Yard Fight was about what the songs were about: he wanted to stop singing about football and stop bragging about straight edge. Of the firing, he said it wasn't like kicking Jimmy Page out of Zeppelin, just "a dude playing power chords."

The new band wrote itself rules. No wearing old shirts to brag, only new band shirts. No X imagery, even though the members all put X's on their hands. No songs directly about straight edge. And everybody moves on stage. A full set from The Rat in Boston, September 14, 1997, is on video.

years.h: Several thousand demos sell before anyone signs the band
years.p: Every song is new; nothing carries over from Ten Yard Fight. Revelation says the demo sold several thousand copies before the band signed.
years.xp:
Pappalardo says the band wrote the demo, recorded it and was playing live and tight within two months. Labels they liked came calling, and the choice was easy: "Bulldog or Star? C'mon...it was sick as fuck."

He still thinks the demo versions beat the album ones.

eras.title: Pushead on the cover
eras.text: Revelation signed the band, and The Difference Between came with a cover by the man who drew for Metallica and SSD. Then Revelation put In My Eyes in a van with its West Coast and Boston bands for the summer.

years.h: Pushead draws the cover of The Difference Between
years.p: Revelation REV 67 has ten new songs plus reworked demo tracks, recorded at Salad Days in Boston with [[Brian McTernan|eda2cb2f-b2c6-4e74-9fd7-49ea52df4172]] of [[Battery|172d89ba-95ab-4e30-92a2-fe836ba0601e]]. First pressing: 213 yellow and 104 red.
years.xp:
Pushead had drawn for [[Metallica|65f4f0c5-ef9e-490c-aee3-909e7ae6b2ab]], the [[Misfits|936addc3-91aa-49de-8ec0-0dc186de151f]] and [[SSD|ee3fc3fc-1b89-423c-8310-bd06c10616ee]], and he reached out to Pappalardo himself. "He offered to do art for us, which ruled." Everyone assumed the cover would be a live photo or a drawing of some guy moshing. Pushead proposed a black die-cut sleeve that shows only the eyes at first.

Pappalardo later called the album too dry and polished next to the demo.

years.cap: In My Eyes live to a packed floor, late 1990s
years.h: A summer on the road with Revelation's other bands
years.p: In My Eyes join [[Speak 714|843e9ff5-c56d-4262-97d1-ae4f82d7e635]], [[Better Than a Thousand|9a5d50be-8dff-4f2f-8852-aa4eafb8f985]] and [[Battery|172d89ba-95ab-4e30-92a2-fe836ba0601e]] on a Revelation package, on top of weekend runs out of Boston.
years.xp: "We played every weekend, somewhere," Pappalardo says. Touring was mostly a summer thing, and the band probably played Boston proper only about ten times.

eras.title: Nothing to Hide, then enough
eras.text: Down to one guitar, the band made a heavier, catchier second album, covered a D.C. band from the Dischord catalog, took it to Europe, and ended it all on National Edge Day.

q: Some people complained about the album being more melodic, which is trippy to me.
yt: Fox News Boston on straight edge, August 3, 1999
years.h: Brian McTernan won't let In My Eyes use reverb
years.p: Nothing to Hide, Revelation REV 80, is heavier and catchier, with one guitar after Jeff Neumann's exit. It includes a cover of [[Faith|f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574]]'s What's Wrong With Me?.
years.xp:
Pappalardo wanted heavier riffs, catchier songs and better lyrics, and wished the album had more reverb: "Why the fuck was everyone so afraid of reverb? Brian legit wouldn't let us use it." Some fans said it was too melodic. The breakdown in On My Side was not standard youth crew. He also credits Garro for working hard on it; you can hear the energy.

Revelation's first pressing was 500 white and 220 clear, and a second of 330 blue was sold on the European tour. In August 1999 a Fox News Boston crew filmed a segment on straight edge with the band.

years.h: In My Eyes stops on National Edge Day, 2000
years.p: The band plays its last show in October 2000, on the second National Edge Day. Pappalardo says anything more would have been overkill.
years.xp:
"There was a mini-hardcore recession and it was a weird time," Pappalardo says. "Everyone needed to do their own thing. I'm cool with that."

Members went on to The Explosion (Genuardi on bass), Fastbreak and Panic. Pappalardo became a writer, including the hardcore book Radio Silence.

eras.title: Back in the Middle East
eras.text: Revelation kept both albums in print on new colors of vinyl. The band played a Revelation anniversary showcase in 2012 and came back in 2015 for a sold-out Boston benefit.

years.cap: In My Eyes at the Revelation 25th Anniversary Showcase, The Glasshouse, June 10, 2012
years.h: Revelation reissues both albums in new colors
years.p: Revelation presses 513 purple copies of The Difference Between and 556 green of Nothing to Hide, then 550 clear and 330 grey in 2013.
years.xp: The band is back on a stage the same year: the Revelation Records 25th Anniversary Showcase at The Glasshouse, June 10, 2012. hate5six films a full set that August.

years.cap: In My Eyes at the Revelation 25th Anniversary Showcase, The Glasshouse, June 10, 2012
years.h: Sweet Pete plays a cover he couldn't manage at thirteen
years.p: In My Eyes play a sold-out benefit for longtime Boston scene member Jarrod Shanahan at the Middle East in Cambridge, with [[The Rival Mob|06f73938-04f9-4b08-adc3-2978bb957de9]] and Boston Strangler. Tickets are $20; resellers ask $60.
years.xp:
Sweet Pete told the crowd, "I stand on this song because I couldn't play it in my first punk band at 13 years old." The upstairs hall held about 200 and was packed.

Two bands, Stay Accused and So Be It, dropped off the bill, and The Rival Mob and Boston Strangler closed by trading the stage every few songs for about 40 minutes.

years.h: Where It Went spends two hours on Nothing to Hide
years.p: Sweet Pete, Pappalardo and Genuardi take the album apart for episode 80 of the podcast, which works through the Revelation catalog record by record.
